doc.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018

title: The story behind 'Truth in Blue'
summary: She explains the melodic arc as repeated attempts at a relationship ending in acceptance of truth.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well there’s more to that. That’s actually the piece of another story. In the very beginning it has the melody [hums]. And then comes that line [hums]. So that’s the whole arc. And the arc tells a story. So in the very beginning there are those three lines, right? And what happened for me is that I kept hearing those three lines playing in my head over and over and over again, like for months. It was crazy. And I felt like the notes had a story but I had to try to figure it out or else I couldn’t write the rest of the song. So then when I sat down with the melody and I thought oh my goodness, all of a sudden it made sense to me. The melody starts the same but the ending has slight variations. And the first line basically represented we are starting a relationship. It doesn’t necessarily mean that it’s romantic. It can be. But it can be friendship. At the time it was friendship for me. And you start it and it doesn’t quite work out the way you want it to, but it’s not bad, it just

didn’t, you know, something went — and then you try it again and then it really goes left on you. And that’s when you maybe have the bad break-up. And then you have the third time, you try it again, and then there’s [hums] and what you have is like a moment of acceptance, where it resolves. And then the line [hums] is just whatever the next phase in life is but it keeps playing over and over again until you find the solution that you have to accept. And so the song is called “Truth In Blue” because you hear about white lies and you hear about bad lies, there’s all these different shades of what a lie is. But ultimately a lie is a lie. And I believe the same thing applies to truth. We try to come up with all these different versions of truth. “Oh maybe, I don’t know, I mean it could have worked out but maybe it was just —” and you know you make all these excuses because we don’t want to accept the truth about something, because the truth is just, we cannot feel resolution in that. We are not satisfied with it. But the thing is until you accept the truth about something you will continue to repeat it over and over again, regardless if that truth is something that you want to accept or not. You will continue to experience it. And you will never feel rest. And so that’s why that note does that. And that’s why the song ends with that as well. Because at the end of the song we don’t know if I’ve gotten it yet. So that’s what that is. That seems a bit brainy but, not all songs are like that.

That’s a great backstory to that. Anyway and I love the way the song just starts out with just you and there’s nothing like a little bit of something to listen to to capture your attention, at least that’s the way I feel. What’s going to come next, as opposed to everybody starting together.
